records.title: The Rust Reference — Inline assembly — Options
supports: nomem: 'The assembly code does not read from or write to any memory accessible outside of the assembly code. This allows the compiler to cache the values of modified global variables in registers across execution of the assembly code' — hence sti/cli/hlt blocks that bracket interrupt handlers must not carry nomem
nostack: the block does not push to the stack or write the red zone
preserves_flags: the block does not modify the flags register
records.limits: normative for the language; the kernel's use is ADR-0010 item 10

records.title: Fuchsia / Zircon kernel concepts — Handles
supports: a handle is a per-process 32-bit value naming a kernel object together with rights; 0 is ZX_HANDLE_INVALID
rights belong to the handle, not the object: two handles to one object may differ; duplication may reduce rights
kernel objects are reference counted, each handle holds a reference; the kernel may reuse the integer values of closed handles
records.limits: design reference only (no code reuse); nawah adds a generation to the value so stale handles are refused deterministically

records.title: Fuchsia / Zircon syscall reference — zx_channel_write
supports: channel handle needs ZX_RIGHT_WRITE; each transferred handle needs ZX_RIGHT_TRANSFER
limits ZX_CHANNEL_MAX_MSG_BYTES 65536 and ZX_CHANNEL_MAX_MSG_HANDLES 64 (nawah: 4096 and 4 per PLAN §4)
ZX_ERR_PEER_CLOSED when the other end is closed; ZX_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED when the channel's own handle is in the handle array; duplicates in the array are ZX_ERR_BAD_HANDLE
records.limits: Zircon discards sent handles on failure too; nawah's contract keeps the sender's table untouched on failure (two-phase write)

records.version: secondary summary read 2026-10-18 (PCIe Base Specification §7.2.2 and PCI Local Bus 3.0 §6.1/§6.7 are PCI-SIG member documents)

records.title: Microsoft Extensible Firmware Initiative FAT32 File System Specification (fatgen103)
records.version: version 1.03 (Microsoft .doc); field layout cross-read from the ELM Chan 'FAT Filesystem' page (elm-chan.org/docs/fat_e.html) on 2026-10-18
supports: BPB offsets: BytsPerSec 11, SecPerClus 13, RsvdSecCnt 14, NumFATs 16, RootEntCnt 17 (0 on FAT32), TotSec16 19 (0), FATSz16 22 (0), TotSec32 32, FATSz32 36, ExtFlags 40, FSVer 42, RootClus 44, FSInfo 48, BkBootSec 50, BootSig 66 = 0x29, VolLab 71, FilSysType 82, signature 0x55AA at 510
FirstDataSector = RsvdSecCnt + NumFATs * FATSz32; FirstSectorOfCluster(N) = (N-2) * SecPerClus + FirstDataSector; FAT type by cluster count (FAT32 >= 65525)

FAT32 entries: low 28 bits (free 0, chain 2..0x0FFFFFF6, bad 0x0FFFFFF7, EOC >= 0x0FFFFFF8), high 4 bits preserved; FAT[0] low byte = media, FAT[1] EOC; FSInfo signatures 0x41615252 / 0x61417272 / 0xAA550000 with free count and next-free hints (0xFFFFFFFF = unknown)

directory entry: Name 0..11, Attr 11 (READ_ONLY 1, HIDDEN 2, SYSTEM 4, VOLUME_ID 8, DIRECTORY 0x10, ARCHIVE 0x20, LONG_NAME 0x0F), FstClusHI 20, FstClusLO 26, FileSize 28; 0xE5 free, 0x00 end, 0x05 for a real 0xE5

records.title: RFC 2104 — HMAC: Keyed-Hashing for Message Authentication
supports: HMAC = H(K XOR opad, H(K XOR ipad, text)); ipad = 0x36 × B, opad = 0x5C × B, B = 64 for SHA-256-class block sizes; keys longer than B are hashed first (§2)
truncation keeps the leftmost t bits, t ≥ max(L/2, 80) (§5)
records.limits: B = 64 for SHA-256 follows FIPS 180-4's block size; RFC 4231 supplies the SHA-256 vectors

records.title: RFC 4231 — Identifiers and Test Vectors for HMAC-SHA-224/256/384/512
supports: HMAC-SHA-256 test cases 1–7 (§4): TC1 key 0x0b×20 / "Hi There" → b0344c61…2e32cff7; TC2 "Jefe" / "what do ya want for nothing?" → 5bdcc146…64ec3843; TC6 key 0xaa×131 → 60e43159…0ee37f54; TC7 key 0xaa×131 long data → 9b09ffa7…5c3a35e2
records.limits: TC5 is a truncated (128-bit) output and is not used; TC3/TC4 (0xaa/0xdd and 0x01..0x19/0xcd patterns) are not in the self-test

records.title: RFC 8018 — PKCS #5: Password-Based Cryptography Specification Version 2.1
supports: PBKDF2 (§5.2): l = CEIL(dkLen/hLen), T_i = F(P,S,c,i) = U_1 XOR … XOR U_c, U_1 = PRF(P, S || INT(i)), U_j = PRF(P, U_{j-1}), INT(i) four-octet big-endian, DK = T_1 || … || T_l truncated to dkLen
salt at least 8 octets (§4.1); iteration count minimum 1000 following SP 800-132, as large as acceptable (§4.2); HMAC-SHA-256 as PRF (appendix B.1.2, id-hmacWithSHA256)
records.limits: the RFC carries no PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 vectors; RFC 7914 §11 supplies them

records.title: RFC 7914 — The scrypt Password-Based Key Derivation Function, §11 test vectors for PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256
supports: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256("passwd", "salt", c=1, dkLen=64) = 55ac046e…d3a19783
PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256("Password", "NaCl", c=80000, dkLen=64) = 4ddcd8f6…97f33c8d
records.limits: only the two PBKDF2 vectors are used; scrypt itself is not implemented

records.title: NIST SP 800-132 — Recommendation for Password-Based Key Derivation, Part 1: Storage Applications
records.version: December 2010 (final; NIST planning note 2023-05-11 announces a revision)
supports: salt: the randomly generated portion shall be at least 128 bits, from an approved RBG (§5.1)
iteration count: a minimum of 1,000 is recommended; 10,000,000 may be appropriate for critical keys (§5.2)
PBKDF2 with HMAC and any approved hash function is the approved PBKDF (§5.3); kLen at least 112 bits (§5)
